gaps.title: Finance administrator role and Delete visibility for other users undefined
gaps.description: DEC-001 settles that only finance administrators delete invoices and other users cannot. What a finance administrator is, how the role is assigned or removed, and what a non-administrator sees in place of the row Delete button are not defined. The capture shows Delete visibly enabled on the row with no indication of which role the screen was viewed as.
gaps.why_it_matters: Deletion of financial records is restricted to one role; without a defined role and assignment rule the restriction cannot be specified or enforced, and the mockup's always-enabled Delete gives no guidance for other users.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Unauthorised users could delete invoices, or the role could be implemented inconsistently between the interface and the server.

gaps.title: Deleting issued or paid invoices and permanent purge versus record-retention obligations
gaps.description: It is not stated whether Delete is allowed for invoices in every status (draft, issued, paid). DEC-003 says deleted invoices are removed permanently after 30 days; whether this permanent removal is compatible with legal or accounting retention obligations for issued invoices is unresolved.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[0] (SCR-002) 'Is Delete permitted for every invoice regardless of status'

gaps.why_it_matters: Invoices are financial records shown in GBP; permanently removing issued or paid invoices 30 days after deletion may breach statutory retention duties and breaks the accounting trail for the customer named on the invoice.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The product could irreversibly destroy records the business is legally required to keep, exposing it to compliance penalties and unreconcilable accounts.
research_questions: How long must UK businesses retain issued VAT invoices under HMRC rules, and does that permit deleting an issued invoice?
How do established accounting products (for example Xero, QuickBooks Online) treat deletion of draft versus issued or paid invoices?

gaps.title: Recovery of deleted invoices not covered by the mockup; who may recover is unanswered
gaps.description: REQ-006 (must) and DEC-003 require deleted invoices to be recoverable for 30 days. No screen, component or flow in the capture supports finding or recovering a deleted invoice. DEC-004 restates the 30-day window but does not say who may recover an invoice, whether deleted invoices remain visible during the window, or how the remaining time is communicated.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-004 verbatim (does not name who recovers)

gaps.why_it_matters: Recovery is a must-have and the only safeguard against mistaken deletion of an invoice; without a defined recovery path and permission it cannot be specified or tested.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Mistakenly deleted invoices may be unrecoverable in practice, or recoverable by users who should not be able to restore financial records.
research_questions: How do established business applications present soft-deleted records during a fixed retention window and communicate the date of permanent removal?

gaps.title: Excel export not shown in the mockup; scope, content and audience undefined
gaps.description: DEC-002 confirms both PDF and Excel exports are needed (REQ-004, must). The capture shows only an Export PDF row action. Whether Excel export is per invoice or for many invoices, which fields it contains, and which users may use it are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: A must-have export format has no supporting interface or defined content, and the export will carry user-entered values such as customer names into a spreadsheet.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Excel export may be omitted, built at the wrong scope, expose data to the wrong users, or produce spreadsheets with unsafe cell content.
research_questions: What does OWASP guidance on CSV and formula injection require for spreadsheet exports that contain user-entered text fields?
What columns do established invoicing products include in Excel exports of invoice lists?

gaps.title: Delete confirmation and post-delete feedback not shown
gaps.description: The capture does not show whether Delete asks for confirmation, what the user is told about the 30-day recovery window, or what is shown after a successful or failed delete.
gaps.why_it_matters: Delete removes a financial record from the list with a single row button next to Export PDF, so a misclick is plausible; users need to know the record is recoverable and for how long.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Accidental deletions, user uncertainty about whether deletion is reversible, and unhandled delete failures.
research_questions: How does WCAG 2.2 success criterion 3.3.4 (Error Prevention: Legal, Financial, Data) apply to deleting financial records that remain recoverable for a period?

gaps.title: Audit trail for deletion, recovery and permanent purge undefined
gaps.description: No requirement says whether deleting, recovering, permanently purging or exporting an invoice must be recorded (who, what, when).
gaps.why_it_matters: Only one role may delete invoices and records are purged after 30 days; without a trace there is no way to show who removed a financial record or to investigate a disputed deletion.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Deletions and purges of invoices cannot be attributed or audited.
research_questions: What audit-trail expectations do UK accounting record-keeping rules (for example HMRC Making Tax Digital) place on deleting or altering invoice records?

gaps.title: PDF export content, permissions, delivery and failure behaviour undefined
gaps.description: For Export PDF it is not defined who may use it, what the PDF contains beyond the three visible fields, whether it downloads or opens, and what happens on failure. Whether a deleted invoice can still be exported during the recovery window is also undefined.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-002 (does not say who uses each format)

gaps.why_it_matters: The PDF is the customer-facing form of the invoice; its content and audience determine whether it is a valid invoice document and who can extract invoice data.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Exported PDFs may lack required invoice details or be available to the wrong users.
research_questions: What information must a UK VAT invoice contain under HMRC rules?

gaps.title: Related records and invoice statuses on delete and purge undefined
gaps.description: What happens to records linked to an invoice (for example payments or credit notes) when it is deleted, recovered or purged, and which invoice statuses exist beyond the captured row, are not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[0] (SCR-002) 'what happens to related records' and 'What invoice statuses ... exist'

gaps.why_it_matters: Recovery within 30 days and purge afterwards both need a defined effect on anything that references the invoice.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Orphaned or inconsistent linked records after deletion or purge, or recovered invoices missing their history.

gaps.title: Row action buttons lack column label and invoice-specific names
gaps.description: The actions column is unlabeled and each row's buttons are named only Delete and Export PDF, without identifying which invoice they act on.
gaps.why_it_matters: With many rows, screen reader users would hear repeated 'Delete' buttons with no invoice context, raising the risk of deleting the wrong invoice.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Accessibility non-conformance and a higher chance of deleting or exporting the wrong invoice.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria (for example 1.3.1, 2.4.6, 4.1.2) govern accessible names for repeated per-row action buttons and unlabeled table columns?

gaps.title: Empty, loading and error states of the invoices table not shown
gaps.description: Only a default state with one invoice row was captured; what the table shows with no invoices, while loading, or when loading fails is not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: The invoices table is the entry point for delete and both exports; after deleting the last invoice the list becomes empty.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Inconsistent or missing states built ad hoc, including after deletion empties the list.
research_questions: How does WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages) apply to loading and error states of a data table?

gaps.title: Behaviour with many invoices (search, sort, pagination) not shown
gaps.description: Only one invoice row was captured; behaviour with many invoices, and whether an Excel export of many invoices follows the current list view, is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Finance administrators need to find a specific invoice to delete or export, and multi-invoice export scope may depend on the list view.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The list may not scale and export scope may be unclear.

gaps.title: Concurrent and repeated delete or recovery actions undefined
gaps.description: It is not defined what happens when two administrators act on the same invoice at once (for example one deletes while another exports or recovers it), or when Delete is triggered twice.
gaps.why_it_matters: Deletion starts a 30-day clock; stale views or repeated requests could restart, skip or misreport that window.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Confusing errors, inconsistent recovery deadlines or exports of already-deleted invoices.
research_questions: What established patterns make delete and restore operations on soft-deleted records idempotent under concurrent requests?

gaps.title: Currencies and number formats in invoices and exports undefined
gaps.description: Only a GBP amount was captured; whether other currencies exist and how amounts are formatted in the table, PDF and Excel exports is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Excel exports in particular need amounts as usable numbers with a clear currency, not only formatted text.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Exported amounts may be ambiguous or unusable for calculation.

assumptions.text: The business operates in the UK, inferred from the £ amount on the captured invoice.
assumptions.why: Retention, invoice-content and audit research questions need a jurisdiction.
assumptions.impact: Research questions in GAP-002, GAP-006 and GAP-007 name HMRC rules.
assumptions.to_confirm: The jurisdictions whose invoicing and record-retention rules apply.

assumptions.text: DEC-001 ('other users cannot delete') overrides the rule in REQ-002 even though REQ-002 is recorded as approved, so no gap is raised for creators deleting their own invoices.
assumptions.why: REQ-002 is approved in the registry while the decision text contradicts it.
assumptions.impact: Creator-based deletion is treated as out of scope.
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether REQ-002 should be superseded by DEC-001.

assumptions.text: DEC-003 is read as: a deleted invoice is kept and recoverable for 30 days, then removed permanently, reconciling REQ-005 and REQ-006.
assumptions.why: Both requirements are approved and the decision combines them.
assumptions.impact: No conflict gap is raised between REQ-005 and REQ-006.
assumptions.to_confirm: That permanent removal happens automatically at the end of the 30 days.

proposed_status_changes.reason: DEC-004 does not say who may recover a deleted invoice or how recovery is reached; no recovery path is in the capture.
DEC-002 confirms Excel export but not its scope, contents or which users may use it; no Excel export is in the capture.
The finance administrator role and how it is assigned are not defined.
